stories.headline: Tata Sons board unanimous on panel for RBI compliance
stories.deck: Trusts Chairman Noel Opposed IPO, Backed Other Options
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Even as 
Tata Sons
 board members remained divided on the reappointment of 
N Chandrasekaran
 as chairman, they were unanimous on the need to form a committee to examine options for complying with RBI's regulations for upper-layer NBFCs, people aware of the matter said. People privy to the discussions said there was no resolution on an IPO at Thursday's board meeting and no vote by directors on the matter. But Tata Sons directors across the board agreed that a team with representatives from Tata Sons, Tata Trusts and independent external members would need to engage with the central bank, Tata Trusts and other stakeholders to evolve a roadmap for compliance.
The decision followed questions from Tata Trusts chairman and Tata Sons director Noel Tata on how the company intended to proceed and explore avenues to avoid a public listing. RBI rules require upper-layer NBFCs with assets above Rs 1 lakh crore, or with direct or indirect access to public funds, to list. Tata Sons had assets of Rs 2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026, double the threshold.
What advisory firm institutional investors said
The decision taken was that the proposed committee's findings and recommendations would be presented to the board for consideration, following which an appropriate course of action will be determined. 
Noel also communicated to the board that the RBI regulations that require upper-layer NBFCs, a category in which Tata Sons falls, to list allow such entities to exit the regulatory framework if they voluntarily restructure their operations.
However, a corporate restructuring expert pointed out that merging an operating Tata company such as TCS with Tata Sons could help it exit RBI's upper-layer NBFC framework but may erode its valuation premium as investors grapple with whether to value it as an IT company or a conglomerate holding company.
The other option is to split Tata Sons into two entities, which could alter its regulatory classification and potentially remove the requirement for an IPO. Barring Noel Tata, the rest of the Tata Sons board believes compliance with RBI's regulations would entail a mandatory stock market listing after the central bank rejected Tata Sons' application to voluntarily surrender its certificate of registration, which had been pending for more than two years.
A public listing is expected to unlock value for shareholders, especially the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Tata Sons' largest minority investor, while giving the holding company of the 
Tata Group
 greater access to capital for businesses such as aviation that require significant investment. But Tata Trusts does not favour a public listing of Tata Sons. Noel Tata told the board that the company would need at least three years to prepare for an IPO if one ultimately becomes unavoidable, citing the extensive corporate, financial and regulatory work involved, including changes to its articles of association, shareholder approvals, financial restatements and due diligence.
He also pointed to the capital commitments and losses at businesses such as Air India and Tata Digital, as well as long-term investments in semiconductors and electronics manufacturing, saying a public issue at this stage could be detrimental to both the company and its shareholders.

stories.headline: ‘Want peace for important deal’: Ex-employee, partner texted family from exec’s phone
stories.deck: Yuvraj Singh Manchanda's family awaits his ashes and belongings after his alleged murder by former colleagues. His body was found and cremated by police before his family was notified. The family claims Haryana Police failed to upload his details promptly on police portals. Suspects sent misleading messages to the family to prolong the deception. Manchanda, a project manager, was preparing for…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: “Our mother is waiting for me to bring back something – anything to remember Yuvraj by. His clothes, his watch… or now, even his ashes,” said Karishma Manchanda, the older sister of Yuvraj Singh Manchanda (31), a project manager at Adani Realty, who was killed allegedly by two of his former colleagues, his body dumped in a drain in Gurgaon.
While his body was found by Haryana Police on Sept 10, the family didn’t find out till Sept 16
.  His body had been cremated by cops in the interim. Karishma said her family has still not been given his remains. She told TOIit was only when she went to the Badshahpur police station in Gurgaon on Sept 16 that she realised her brother’s body had been found six days ago and had already been cremated.
According to Delhi Police, Yuvraj was murdered by Anya Vats and Sanyam Sachdeva, his former colleagues at a real estate firm, on Sept 6.
His family eventually learnt that he had died after Delhi Police apprehended Vats and Sachdeva from Uttarakhand, following which they confessed to their crime.
The family alleged that Haryana Police did not follow protocol and didn’t upload Yuvraj’s photo on Zipnet — a portal used by police in different states to share information about missing or unknown dead persons.
After they filed the missing complaint, the family and friends checked Zipnet every day for any information. 
Details of missing or unknown deceased persons are uploaded on Zipnet or CCTNS for family members to identify them. “Every hour of the day, we would check Zipnet. There was no update,” said Rajat Jain.
Karishma and one of Yuvraj’s friends, Sahil, went to Badshahpur police station on Sept 16. “We saw Yuvraj’s picture. Police said he was found in a drain on Sept 10. We were shocked to hear that his body had been cremated by police on Sept 14,” Sahil said.
Haryana Police, as per the information on Zipnet, uploaded his details only on Sept 16. They, however, said Zipnet was not the principal pan-India system being used for unidentified bodies and maintained the details were uploaded on CCTNS as part of the prescribed process on Sept 11. “Had the information been uploaded on Zipnet as soon as they found his body, at least we would have been able to perform his last rites and grieve,” Jain said.
Karishma, meanwhile, also said she was made to wait for five hours when she went to Badshahpur police station for information about her dead brother’s belongings. After two days, the family is yet to receive anything — his ashes, clothes, a 
kada
, his gold ring or even the postmortem report. Sahil said police told them that they had “given away” his clothes, as they were “stinking”.
Suspects sent his family texts
For two days after they saw him last on Sept 6, Karishma and her parents received messages from Yuvraj Singh Manchanda’s phone telling them he was working on an “important deal” and wanted “peace”. He refused to take their calls. A message on Sept 7 said he was flying to Bengaluru for work that day, along with a photo of a ticket. The last message came a day later, asking them not to disturb him and saying that he would call two days later.
Only, Yuvraj had been killed on Sept 6. The promised call never came and Yuvraj’s family hit the panic button on Sept 11, filing a missing person complaint at Delhi’s Lajpat Nagar police station.
According to Delhi Police, it was Vats and Sachdeva who kept sending messages to Yuvraj’s family members and friends to keep the ruse alive and prevent them from approaching the police.
Karishma recalled that when she received his messages after Sept 6, she begged him to call, show his face or even send a voice note. “My younger sister got a message saying he would call her on Sept 10. When his phone was switched off on that day, we panicked and filed a missing persons complaint,” she said.
A project manager at Adani Realty, Yuvraj was described by his friends as a passionate and dedicated employee. Hours before he disappeared, he had bought a sherwani from Lajpat Nagar for his wedding, which was scheduled for Oct.
“Our mother is a heart patient and our father is paralysed. Yuvraj would come back by 10pm every day to take care of them. Now, we can only hope of getting his ashes home,” Karishma said.

stories.headline: Karnataka, NLSIU sign MoU for prison reforms
stories.deck: Karnataka, NLSIU sign MoU for prison reforms
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: Karnataka’s Department of Prisons and Correctional Services and the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) have signed an MoU to strengthen legal aid and support prison reforms in the state..The MoU was signed at the prisons headquarters in Bengaluru in the presence of Alok Kumar, Director General of Police, Prisons and Correctional Services, and Advocate Ragini Ahuja, Co-Director, Criminal Justice Clinic, NLSIU..Under the agreement, NLSIU’s Criminal Justice Clinic, through its lawyers, students and researchers, will identify elderly prisoners and those suffering from serious ailments and assist them in securing their release, wherever legally applicable..The clinic will also organise legal aid camps in prisons and provide pro bono legal representation to marginalised accused persons in custody..Technical measures underway to address network jammer issues around Mangaluru prison: Priyank Kharge.Premature release.It will assist the prisons department in drafting a policy for the premature release of elderly and terminally ill prisoners in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions. The clinic will also undertake research and assist in drafting laws and policies related to prisons in Karnataka..As part of the collaboration, NLSIU will support capacity building of para-social workers, convict lawyers and lawyers working in prisons. It will assist the department in other activities aimed at prison reforms and provide training to prison staff and students involved in the activities.

stories.headline: Bihar announces OTS scheme for brick kilns, waives ₹90 crore interest on outstanding dues
stories.deck: Interest component will be waived off under OTS; It will benefit around 6000 brick kiln owners. It will be applicable for three months beginning Sep 21.
stories.bodyText:
Bihar government on Friday (September 18, 2026) came out with a One-Time Settlement (OTS) scheme for the settlement of outstanding dues of brick kilns for brick kiln season 2024-25.
Under the scheme, brick kiln owners will have to deposit outstanding principal dues, while the interest component, which had accumulated on their earlier dues, will be waived off by the State government, Mr. Kumar told reporters at his official chamber at Vikas Bhawan.
He added that brick kiln owners owe a total of ₹316.66 crore, comprising ₹226.40 crore in outstanding royalty and ₹90.26 crore in interest.
Out of ₹316.66 crore outstanding dues, only ₹27.28 crore has been recovered by the District Mining Officers concerned through certificate proceedings/FIRs, thus leaving ₹289.38 crore as outstanding amount that includes ₹203 crore as principal amount while ₹85 crore as interest component.
“In Bihar, those engaged in the brick-kiln business had a substantial amount of money outstanding with the government for a long period. They had also been demanding that arrangements be made for them to pay the outstanding amount in a lump sum. We considered their plea and, accordingly, the state cabinet, in its last meeting, decided to bring an OTS scheme for those engaged in the business of brick kilns in the State,” Mr. Kumar said while speaking to the press in Patna.
“I would like to thank the Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for bringing the scheme under which a one-time payment can be made, and substantial relief has been provided to those engaged in the brick-kiln business,” he said, adding that the move will increase the government’s revenue, while also providing considerable relief to people engaged in this business.
The scheme will be applicable for a period of three months between September 21 and December 20, 2026, during which brick kiln owners will have to deposit the entire amount, failing which they will have to pay the entire dues under the earlier system, including the full interest. There are people associated with approximately 6,000 brick kilns.
The minister appealed to all the brick-kiln owners to deposit the one-time amount within the stipulated period so that they can restart their businesses afresh and do not face any difficulties in the future.
Changes in rules
While talking about the department approving “Bihar District Mineral Foundation (Amendment) Rules 2026 that brought certain changes in the earlier 2018 Rules, Mr. Kumar said that 2% amount is deposited in each district from where mineral extraction takes place, where minerals such as stone or sand are excavated. A district associated with mining receives this two per cent amount.
Following the amendments to the Rules, 70% of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) will be spent in the block from where the minerals are being extracted, while 30% will be spent in other blocks of the district, Mr. Kumar said, adding that earlier, the ratio was 60:40.
Another change is that elected members such as Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assembly, and Members of Legislative Council from different districts were previously not members of the District Mineral Foundation (DMF), the Minister said, adding that they will now also be members of the DMF following the change in the Rules.
He asserted that the auction of stone-mining areas has also been completed in Nawada and Sheikhpura and the auction in other districts will be carried out as quickly as possible.
The Minister said that Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Satish Chandra Dubey will be visiting the state on September 22 (2026) and “we will have a meeting with the Geological Survey of India (GSI) along with him. Our objective is to move forward in the mineral sector as quickly as possible and expedite the work.

stories.headline: How UK-returned MTech graduate plotted boy’s abduction and murder
stories.deck: How UK-returned MTech graduate plotted boy’s abduction and murder
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: A few months ago, Vaka Bhaskar Reddy returned to Bengaluru after graduating with an MTech degree from the United Kingdom. Now, he is the prime suspect in the abduction of a 13-year-old boy, allegedly to secure money to clear his father’s Rs 3-crore debt..Reddy, 28, who was arrested on Wednesday, was working in the finance department of a multinational conglomerate in Whitefield. He joined the company a month ago on a pay package of about Rs 65,000 a month, but had not yet drawn his first salary..Reddy meticulously planned for a week to kidnap and murder his neighbour’s son and demand Rs 1 crore as a ransom to give to his father, who wasn’t involved in the crime..Investigations revealed that Reddy targeted his neighbours as they were well-to-do. “The victim’s father had a good reputation and made decent money in real estate. They owned their house and vehicles. The family had moved to the city from Nellore in Andhra Pradesh some time ago,” a senior police officer told DH..Gurugram realtor murder: Wedding plans, unanswered calls and a cremation that left family seeking answers.But this was not a standard kidnap-for-ransom plan. Reddy, after cajoling the child into his car, took him to an abandoned layout in Bagalur and brutally murdered him. Before this, he recorded a 90-second video of the child requesting his father to pay the ransom or he would be killed. Reddy had planned to send it to the boy’s parents the following day..“It was premeditated. Reddy never intended to let go of the child, as it would lead to his identification. He instead planned to lure him away, record the video, kill him and dispose of the body before demanding the ransom using the video. No ransom phone call was made. The suspect’s plans were foiled the moment he was involved in two accidents and was caught,” the officer said..Reddy’s father, who was unaware of his son’s plans, had helped the victim’s father search for the missing child before they had approached the police on the evening of September 17..“The two families knew each other well,” another officer said.

briefs.headline: Krishna Byre Gowda raps BDA engineer for failing to clear debris
briefs.deck: Minister raps BDA engineer for failing to clear debris
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Friday pulled up an assistant executive engineer (AEE) of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) for failing to ensure the removal of debris near Hebbal flyover, questioning whether officials were working for the public or contractors..During an inspection of areas cleared under the ‘Freedom from Waste’ campaign near the flyover, the minister directed officials to ensure that waste was cleared completely and that the reclaimed spaces were put to public use..Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar launches 'Freedom from Waste' campaign in Bengaluru.“Are you working for the people or for contractors?” Gowda reportedly asked BDA AEE Vijay Reddy, while expressing displeasure over the failure to clear waste from the area. The minister said the objective of the campaign was not merely to remove accumulated waste, but to reclaim such spaces for public use..The remarks come at a time when the BDA had claimed to have cleared several thousand tonnes of waste from public places in recent months as part of the special campaign.

briefs.headline: India rejects Pakistan’s allegations regarding collision of Indian, Pak ships in Arabian Sea
briefs.deck: The incident happened on the night of September 15, when a Pakistani vessel closed in on a frontline Indian Navy warship that was on a routine surveillance mission in the north Arabian Sea
briefs.bodyText:
India on Friday (September 18, 2026) strongly rejected Islamabad’s allegations with respect to a collision between a Pakistani vessel and an Indian Navy warship in the Arabian Sea.
New Delhi on Wednesday (September 16) summoned the Pakistani Chargé d'Affaires (CDA) and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable conduct” by the Pakistan Navy vessel that led to the collision.
The incident happened on Tuesday night (September 15) after the Pakistani vessel closed in on the frontline Indian Navy warship that was on a routine surveillance mission in the north Arabian Sea, according to the Indian side.
The Pakistani Foreign Ministry had alleged that the incident happened following a “highly provocative and unacceptable action” by the Indian vessel in Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
"We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest we had lodged. It is the usual prevarication that we expected. We reject the allegations and insinuations contained therein," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at his regular media briefing.
The Indian ship INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the western Arabian Sea when the Pakistani naval ship Hunain conducted itself in an “unacceptable and unprofessional manner” at sea, resulting in the collision, he said.
“The dangerous overtaking manoeuvre by PNS Hunain was in gross violation of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991, which specifies that naval units at sea are not to be within three nautical miles of each other. In addition, the Pakistani ship also infringed the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea," Mr. Jaiswal said.
The Pakistan side has once again been “advised” about the need for all military units to exercise due care and to respect the provisions of relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent a repetition of such incidents, he said.
Mr. Jaiswal said the incident did not cause any major damage to INS Kolkata and that she remains at sea.

briefs.headline: Sharad Pawar urges Maharashtra government to declare drought, provide ₹50,000 per hectare relief
briefs.deck: Instead of taking a decision based solely on the average district figures, the actual damage should be considered together based on taluka-wise rainfall, crop condition, and declare drought, says NCP (SP) leader Sharad Pawar
briefs.bodyText:
NCP (SP) leader Sharad Pawar has written to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, urging him to provide relief of ₹50,000 per hectare and declare drought based on the actual damage, taluka-wise rainfall, and crop condition in Maharashtra.
“Instead of taking a decision based solely on the average district figures, the actual damage should be considered together based on taluka-wise rainfall, crop condition, and declare drought,” said Mr. Pawar, adding that the situation is dire in most of the state and in some districts, there is a deficit of about 60% of the average in the last three months.
This year, when looking at the average rainfall deficit by region from June to August, Marathwada has seen a 69% deficit, Vidarbha a 61% deficit, Konkan a 33% deficit and some districts in western and northern Maharashtra a 26% deficit, he stated in the letter.
He listed nine measures, suggesting Mr. Fadnavis to end drought without waiting for formal announcements.
The list includes that farmers should receive ₹50,000 per hectare as an aid, while agricultural labourer families should be given special assistance of ₹25,000 each; the banks should be instructed to expedite the implementation of the loan waiver scheme and increase the incentive subsidy from Rs 50,000 to ₹1 lakh; the announced crop insurance assistance of ₹17,000 per hectare in the unseasonal rains relief package last year should also be distributed immediately, and others.
According to him, at least 31 out of 36 districts in the state have received much less rainfall than the average. The state has received only 748 mm of rainfall from June 1 to September 15, which is a 19% decrease compared to the average.
Mr. Pawar also recommended implementing a one-rupee crop insurance scheme and designing special schemes to be implemented through the Employment Guarantee Scheme. For instance: carry out water conservation and other agricultural-related works.
For livestock, Mr. Pawar has asked to make arrangements of fodder, water, and necessary veterinary services for livestock.
“State and district-level control rooms should be set up to monitor rainfall, crop condition, water scarcity, fodder availability and livestock condition daily in each district. District Collectors should be given the power to make ‘Negative Debit’ to provide additional funds from the treasury,” the letter read.
The other measure includes relief for students by not only waiving examination fees but also the entire educational fees of students studying in schools, colleges and other educational institutions in drought-affected talukas.

briefs.headline: 20 schools, 25,000 students, daily gridlock: Varthur residents lose patience
briefs.deck: 20 schools, 25k kids, daily gridlock: Anger spills over
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Frustration boiled over on the Varthur-Gunjur-Whitefield corridor after school buses took more than two hours to cover barely five kilometres, leaving thousands of children stranded in traffic on Thursday..Helpless parents and residents have now launched a joint representation seeking urgent traffic management and road repairs, stating that prolonged traffic snarls and poor road conditions are severely affecting schoolchildren..According to parents, the road is full of deep craters. There are close to 20 schools along the stretch, with an estimated 15,000 to 25,000 students and 200 to 300 school buses operating daily..“Thousands of students and families depend on this corridor every day. Parents are increasingly experiencing very long school-bus journeys, particularly around the Gunjur Lake/Gunjur stretch,” the representation noted..Parents have sought four immediate measures: heavy-vehicle restrictions, particularly on construction trucks and water tankers during school peak hours; urgent repair of potholes and drainage-related damage; coordinated traffic management around KRDCL work sites; and a joint inspection by Traffic Police, KRDCL, civic authorities and parent-school representatives..Residents told DH that conditions on the ground have turned unbearable..Bengaluru: Commuters question toll on E-City flyover, cite end of 20-year concession period.Varthur Rakshith, Varthur Ward BJP in-charge, said, “Severe and persistent traffic congestion has become a daily problem across the Varthur-Gunjur-Balagere corridor, causing hardships to residents, apartment communities, villagers, schoolchildren, patients travelling to hospitals and thousands of daily commuters.”.A school student said it took two and a half hours to get home across a stretch of less than 4 km. Another student said, “I reach school very late in the morning. Most of the time, I arrive only after the first session.”.Vidyasagar, a resident, said citizens have resorted to filling potholes themselves..“Rama Temple junction, near Candeur Landmark, must be fully asphalted. It’s just 200-300 metres, which makes traffic dead slow due to deep craters. We want the 2-km stretch between Varthur police station and Varthur Kodi to be fully asphalted,” he told DH..He also suggested immediate measures: “Put dividers on SH‑35 main road — there is none between Brigade Utopia and Candeur Landmark. Deploy more traffic personnel, install traffic lights. Introduce direct BMTC buses from the Varthur-Gunjur area to ORR Bellandur via CDP and Panathur underpass, which is the shortest route. Then people would avoid personal cars. Introduce KIA buses to the airport. This will solve traffic, pollution, etc.”.Another resident, Monalisa, said, “Varthur’s problems are not limited to SH‑35. They are multifaceted — traffic and road infrastructure, drainage, pollution, greenery, waste management, pedestrian and school‑bus safety, and broader civic infrastructure all need attention. The approach should therefore be multi‑agency and issue‑specific, rather than treating SH‑35 road expansion alone as the solution.”

briefs.headline: Modern ‘secularism’ is a Western concept, does not fit India: Mohan Bhagwat
briefs.deck: The RSS chief warns against ego, noting India’s historical adherence to dharma, and urges youth to respect their own worship choices while honouring others’ practices
briefs.bodyText:
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday (September 18, 2026) cautioned young people against getting consumed by ego, saying the belief that everything is under one’s control and should happen according to one’s wishes is a misconception.
“Take the example of the Sun. Even if you do not believe in the Sun, it will still rise and set,” Mr. Bhagwat said while speaking at the ‘Yuva Dharma Sansad’ in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh.
He added that people should not live under the illusion that everything operates according to their authority and control and “if there is a rise, there will also be a fall”.
Regarding the definition of secularism, the RSS chief termed it a modern concept that does not fit India’s traditional understanding of the relationship between religion, society and the state.
Non-discrimination
He said India’s approach has traditionally been based on non-discrimination and equal respect for different religious paths, which he described as sarva-pantha-samabhava (equal respect for all religions).
Mr. Bhagwat also urged young people to respect their own chosen form of worship while showing equal respect for the practices of others.
Sharing his understanding of the Western concept of secularism, the RSS chief said it emerged from a historical conflict between kings and religious authorities. “....there was a conflict between kings and religious authorities over who should have power. After much bloodshed, a compromise was reached which was that the king would look after this world, and the religious authorities would look after the other world. So, secular came to mean the material or worldly sphere,” he said adding that India’s tradition seeks both material prosperity and freedom from anger, greed and jealousy, viewing life holistically through dharma.
Hence, “secular does not fit the Indian context”, he pointed out, claiming that “whenever India was governed by Indians, the country followed the path of dharma”.
On global conflicts
Referring to India’s approach to international conflicts, Mr. Bhagwat, without naming Pakistan, said a western neighbour had repeatedly troubled India and that the country had responded when necessary but had not sought to interfere unnecessarily in global conflicts. He said India had helped even those who had caused it difficulties when they faced crises, regardless of the ideology of the government in power.
The ‘Yuva Dharma Sansad’ is being held in Ujjain from September 17 to 19, with organisers claiming participation of around 1,700 youth from across the country.

briefs.headline: North Korea says nuclear status 'irreversible' after UN atomic agency rebuke
briefs.deck: The IAEA’s “biased viewpoint and double standards” are “the fundamental factor causing the collapse of ‌the international nuclear non-proliferation system”, Kim Yo Jong said in a statement ‌in state media KCNA.
briefs.bodyText:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, accused the International Atomic Energy Agency on Saturday (September 19, 2026) of double standards after it adopted a resolution criticising Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons programme.
The IAEA’s “biased viewpoint and double standards” are “the fundamental factor causing the collapse of the international nuclear non-proliferation system”, Kim Yo Jong said in a statement in state media KCNA.
She said the agency had turned a blind eye to the “blatant nuclear proliferation activities” of the United States and South Korea’s “nuclear submarine introduction plan”, while forcibly adopting a resolution against North Korea’s “self-defensive and legitimate nuclear activities”.
In a separate KCNA statement, North Korea’s Foreign Ministry also dismissed the resolution, declaring that its status as a nuclear power is irreversible and backed by its nuclear deterrent.
KCNA also said North Korean leader Kim Jong Un carried out a three-day inspection tour of major munitions factories this week.
Ms. Kim stressed North Korea’s artillery should both fight and deter war with “the most concentrated and destructive, massive and versatile offensive capability”, KCNA said.
Ms. Kim added that North Korea’s efforts to modernise all components of its defence capability are bringing about “a significant change” in the composition and means of its armed forces.
Analysts say North Korea has been overhauling its military with Russian help since the two countries signed a mutual defence treaty in 2024. They say combat experience gained by Pyongyang’s troops deployed to the war in Ukraine has also aided the effort.

stories.headline: Man who attacked wife with floor cleaner in Bengaluru arrested
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A man, who allegedly attacked his 30-year-old wife with a floor cleaner in the basement of a private clinic’s premises in JP Nagar, has been arrested.
Venkatesan (39) was taken to the spot for a mahazar and produced before a court Friday, which remanded him in judicial custody. He has been lodged in the Central Prison at Parappana Agrahara.
His wife Madhumita Maity is still undergoing treatment in the ICU at a private hospital. Police said Venkatesan was injured after being assaulted by people who witnessed the assault. A traffic police sub-inspector caught him.
A senior police officer said Venkatesan confessed that a marital row was the main reason for the attack.
Madhumita’s colleague filed a complaint stating that Venkatesan had visited the clinic a few times in the past and had fought with his wife.
Meanwhile, the Karnataka State Commission for Women has taken suo motu cognisance of the attack. It has written to DCP South, seeking details of the action taken against the accused.

stories.headline: Domestic quarrel turns fatal: Man held for killing wife in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A long-running domestic quarrel and his wife’s failure to answer his phone calls allegedly culminated in murder when a 40-year-old man from Bihar killed his wife at their rented house in Bilekahalli on Sept 16, police said.
After strangling her, the accused allegedly poured hot oil on her face in an attempt to disfigure her and make the death appear to be a suicide. However, discrepancies in his account led police to suspect foul play.
The deceased has been identified as Gunja Maddheshiya, 38, a homemaker, while her husband, Ranjit Kumar Gupta, has been arrested.
According to preliminary investigation, the couple had quarrelled frequently over trivial issues for the past three months. Around 9.30am on Sept 16, Ranjit left for work but returned shortly after and picked another quarrel with Gunja. Both their children had left for school by then. “He assaulted and killed her... Ranjit sat behind her on the floor, put a dupatta around her neck, and strangled her to death,” a senior officer said.
Around 3pm, Ranjit allegedly returned home, heated cooking oil and poured it on Gunja’s face to disfigure her. 
However, her face was not completely burnt. He then closed the door and left for work. Later in the evening, he returned, pretended to be shocked by her death and alerted neighbours, claiming that Gunja had died by suicide.
The house owner learnt about the death around 8pm and told police about the couple’s frequent quarrels. When police inspected the house, Ranjit repeated that his wife had committed suicide. However, police inspector Nataraj DN and his team noticed discrepancies in his account and behaviour. He was detained and questioned.
During questioning, Ranjit allegedly confessed to the crime. He told investigators that he had brought Gunja and their two children from his native place 18 months ago. Their disputes intensified in recent months and Gunja had failed to answer his calls a couple of times, he allegedly told police.
The couple’s son and daughter have been sent to stay with relatives. Ranjit has been remanded in judicial custody.

stories.headline: Bollytech artiste Trapperx to perform in Bengaluru this weekend
stories.deck: Set to perform at Bastian Garden City on September 19, Trapperx aka Sushil Ghunawat talks about his connection with the city and his upcoming performance
stories.bodyText:
Sushil Ghunawat, better known as Bollytech artiste Trapperx, is bringing his All Black Experience with Trapperx to the Bengaluru. The event, that follows the prescribed dress code of all black attire, comes to India after Trapperx’s international tour across Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia.
“The first few viral reels that popularised the name Trapperx were shot in Bengaluru,” says Sushil. His journey from starting out as a gym trainer to becoming the first Indian Bollytech DJ to be featured in New York’s Times Square, without the support of a label, speaks volumes about his effort to bring Indian electronic music to the global stage.
Jaipur-based Sushil worked on his music for over 10 years and taught at a music academy. He has previously performed alongside Shankar Mahadevan, Atif Aslam, Jubin Nautiyal and others, bridging the gap between classical and mainstream Indian music genres with a modern blend of electronic music.
His career as a DJ began with viral reels on social media. Talking about his work, Sushil says, “I was fascinated with techno music, but it did not have a great fan base a couple of years ago. I decided to take original Bollywood tracks that people enjoyed singing along to, and mix them with New Age techno tracks.”
Over the years, he says, almost all the clubs he performed at have welcomed his edits and tracks. “A mashup of ‘Kaho na Kaho’ and ‘Black Dress’ brought me a lot of love and support,” he recalls.
In the past two months, Trapperx has performed in over seven countries and he says the response has been “highly enthusiastic”. The reception to Bollytech music has drastically changed in India with GenZ strongly connecting to it, he says, adding, “Listening to a fresh version of a classic from their childhood has led to older audiences enjoying my work as well. I believe, Bollytech is the next sound from India’s live music industry.”
At the moment, Sushil is working on an audio-visual IP project with a team of over 20 people from across the world in different fields. Probably the biggest IP project ever used by any DJ, Sushil says it is likely to release around November, and will be followed by a launch across India. “Bengaluru has been my biggest supporter; the energy here is amazing. The people love me and my music and it is one of the cities I love returning to.”
The All Black Experience with Trapperx is on September 19 at Bastian Garden City from 9pm to 12:30am. Tickets on SortMyScene

stories.headline: Bengaluru: Minister pulls up officials over waste disposal, re-encroachment
stories.deck: The Minister was inspecting areas surrounding the Hebbal flyover as part of the ‘Freedom from Waste’ campaign on Friday.
stories.bodyText:
Taking on officials once again, Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda asked officials from the Bengaluru North City Corporation whether they were serving the public or siding with the contractor over waste disposal.
The Minister was inspecting areas surrounding the Hebbal flyover as part of the ‘Freedom from Waste’ campaign on Friday (September 18), when he directed officials in the corporation on maintaining public spaces and keeping them free of waste.
Joint inspections
During a virtual meeting later in the day, the Minister also directed civic officials to ensure that footpaths cleared of encroachments do not get occupied again, asking them to form joint teams with the police to monitor the stretches and take action against repeat offenders.
After the Minister was informed that encroachments along 1,373.32 km of arterial and sub-arterial roads have been cleared across five city corporations, he said the focus should now be on preventing the cleared stretches from returning to their earlier condition.
Seize material, register FIRs
Even as street vendors have been demanding that a fresh survey be conducted and vending zones be identified before removing them, the Minister directed officials to register FIRs, seize materials and impose higher penalties on repeat offenders wherever permitted under law.
Inspecting roads near J.P. Nagar Metro station at night, the Minister said he had specifically chosen to inspect the area at night to check whether the street lights were functioning. He said he had repeatedly instructed officials that contractors should be penalised, and officials held accountable, if street lights were not working properly. He added that the area was important as many people use the Metro, and therefore it needed to be well lit. “Despite giving instructions so many times, this is still not the case,” he said.
On road maintenance, he pointed out that some drains had been left open and, at some places, slabs had been placed one over another. “It is common sense. Officials should use common sense,” he said, adding that such basic issues could lead to accidents and should be treated as the officials’ responsibility, especially since they could easily be spotted easily, and hence officials should prioritise these works

briefs.headline: Karnataka govenment, NGO lose appeal in KR Pura land dispute
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In a setback for the state govt and Namma Whitefield RWA Federation Trust, a division bench of Karnataka high court has dismissed their writ appeal over certain parcels of land at Pattanduru Agrahara, KR Pura, which they claimed were part of a tank bed.
On Nov 19, 2025, a single bench dismissed a petition filed by the govt in which the trust had impleaded itself, supporting the petition.
In 2018, the govt challenged a 1980 order of the Bengaluru South taluk land tribunal in favour of KB Munivenkatappa and his family members, citing that the issue was beyond its jurisdiction.
The division bench, comprising Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan, noted that the govt, which was given liberty by an appellate court to challenge the order in Dec 2008, took nine and a half years to file a writ petition in June 2018.
“The state cannot convert the plea of jurisdictional error into an independent means of reopening the entire dispute after having participated in the earlier proceedings and exhausted its appellate remedies. It is also relevant to note that the lower appellate court’s finding was not based solely upon the land tribunal order. The court considered the historical revenue records, as well as the longstanding sale transactions concerning the property,” the division bench said.
“The land in question has been the subject matter of registered transactions commencing from 1918, and an extent of 20 guntas was acquired by the govt on Oct 18, 1931, for a borewell, where the land was shown as ‘dry land’ in the gazette notification published for the acquisition. These facts were part of the records considered in the earlier litigation and cannot now be disregarded while examining the state’s jurisdictional objection,” the division bench observed while rejecting the writ appeals.

briefs.headline: Karnataka HC allows Darshan’s physical presence for cross-examination of key witnesses
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka high court Friday disposed of a petition filed by 
Vijayalakshmi
, wife of Sandalwood actor 
Darshan
, accused no. 2 in the Renukaswamy murder case, permitting his physical production on dates when material witnesses identified by the defence are cross-examined.
Justice V Srishananda directed the trial judge to fix two or three consecutive dates for cross-examination of the material witnesses, in consultation with advocates representing the accused and the special public prosecutor. Once the witnesses appear for cross-examination, the trial judge should allow the physical presence of Darshan and any other accused, if requested.
The court also made it clear that the cross-examination of witnesses must be completed on those dates without seeking adjournments.
Vijayalakshmi had sought a direction for her husband’s physical production on all dates before the trial court, contending that it was a mandatory requirement for a fair trial. Justice Srishananda directed the parties to submit details of the material or key witnesses they relied upon. Lists were subsequently placed before the court.
After considering the submissions, the high court said the prosecution could examine all witnesses it considered material and complete their examination-in-chief, while deferring cross-examination and directing the witnesses to appear on specified dates. 
The prosecution would also have the liberty to decide whether to examine the witnesses named in its list, the court said.
The judge clarified that the directions were specific to this case and should not be treated as a precedent. “The decision in this case shall not be treated as a precedent as the present directions are issued taking note of the sensitivity and peculiarity of the case at hand,” Justice Srishananda said while disposing of the petition.

briefs.headline: SIR: Only 2% of 84L purged voters seek return to electoral rolls in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 With the Sept 23 deadline for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls closing in, only 6.5 lakh of the 84 lakh voters eligible to seek re-inclusion have applied through Forms 6 and 6A.
A total of 1.08 crore names were struck off the draft list after being marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, or refused to sign the enumeration form (ASDDO). Form 6 for resident voters and form 6A for NRIs are the only routes to rejoin the list.
From June 16 to Sept 18, over 6.4 lakh people applied via Form 6, while 4,302 NRI voters used Form 6A. A bulk of these applications came in before citizens received notices over logical discrepancies. Only 1.07 lakh forms were filed after Aug 23, when the ASDDO list was made public.
Excluding dead and duplicate categories, 84 lakh voters figure in absent, shifted and refused-to-sign categories. Against this number, 1.69 lakh applications were filed through Forms 6 and 6A over the past 26 days. Or, just 2% of those who have been issued notices.
Chief electoral officer Anbu Kumar said there is no fixed deadline for submitting Form 6, but those who apply before Sept 23 will make it to the final SIR rolls due on Oct 27, after verification. 
Anyone above 18, of sound mind, an Indian citizen, not barred by law, and not registered as a voter elsewhere in the country can fill Form 6 to get their name added during the SIR process.
The CEO’s office had organised a special enrolment drive at booths on Aug 29 and 30, and a similar drive is set to be held this weekend as authorities make a final push before the window closes.

briefs.headline: SIR hearings: Flexible slots ease voter rush in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The time slot on your SIR notice, it turns out, is more a suggestion than a rule. Across the city, electoral registration officers (EROs) and booth-level officers (BLOs) are hearing cases beyond the printed time, and for many voters that flexibility has come as a relief, even as it strains officials during rush hours.
Shyam Padhi, a Whitefield resident, told 
TOI
 he flagged his unavailability to his BLO, who let a senior family member appear in an earlier slot instead. Even voters who hadn’t received notices yet but spotted their names on the list walked in anyway, and BLOs in some cases let them pick a convenient date.
Pramod Hebbar, who volunteers to help voters navigate SIR at Marathahalli, said mornings see people head to work, so BLOs in his area shifted to a 3pm-6pm slot. “Evenings are relatively light. Hence, in our community, BLOs advised a slot from 3pm to 6pm, and they were helpful in accommodating changes in appointments,” he said.
The leeway varies booth to booth, though, and many voters are still expected to stick to their allotted time. Flexibility mainly kicks in when students must leave town early, when multiple family members get separate notices, or when the slot clashes with work.
Vinu Jade, BLA-2 from New Thippasandra, said such accommodations are largely for senior citizens. “Otherwise, one needs to wait for the time slot allotted,” he said, advising voters to check with their BLO since some booths have fewer notices than others. “If you are a family and go together on one of the many slots given to the members, the BLO will accommodate,” he added.
Vidya Goggi, a citizen committee member assisting RT Nagar voters, said residents there were allowed to walk in early once their documents were ready. “Our hearing centre has allotted different dates to different booths. The schedule is well planned. No one reported any delays or long waiting times,” she said.
Not everyone is pleased, though. An official at the chief electoral officer’s office warned that unscheduled crowds in high-volume regions “could create a chaotic situation”.
An ERO from Bengaluru Central said staff were told to accommodate anyone turning up, since many voters had already missed their dates.
BoxCongress seeks review of SIR process
Ramesh Babu, former Congress MLC and chairman of KPCC media and communications wing, Thursday wrote to Karnataka chief electoral commissioner Anbu Kumar, seeking a statewide review of the SIR process. Citing booth 512 in Yeshwantpur, where only 38% of voters were found valid, he flagged discrepancies statewide and poor response from BLOs, supervisors, AEROs and EROs to grievances. “Administrative difficulties, mapping errors, incomplete enumeration or failure of communication must not result in wrongful exclusion of genuine voters,” he said, seeking a time-bound action report.

briefs.headline: Karnataka govt begins relocation of 11k seized vehicles to Bengaluru outskirts
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Earlier this week, the state govt began the relocation of 11,346 seized or abandoned vehicles lying in and around police stations across the city. As much as 26 acres of govt land has been identified at seven sites on the outskirts of the city for the purpose.
Launching the relocation drive at Jayanagar 4th Block Wednesday, Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said police and revenue departments had worked together to find a long-term solution to the problem that has persisted for over 15 years.
“Many of these vehicles are linked to court cases and cannot simply be disposed of until the cases are resolved. We had made a special request to expedite the process, but the courts have clarified that such cases cannot be fast-tracked,” he said.
With the vehicles unable to be disposed of immediately, police sought alternative land from the revenue department. The identified sites will now be used to park the vehicles, freeing up police station premises and surrounding public spaces.
“Seeing such a scrap-like environment in the middle of a locality is unpleasant. It can also create opportunities for illegal activities. This has been an issue for the police department for 15-20 years. 
We intend to shift as many of these vehicles as possible within the next one month,” he said.
The identified locations are Hagadur village in KR Pura hobli, Yerappanahalli village in Bidarahalli hobli, Hongasandra village in Begur hobli, Thammanayakanahalli village in Kasaba hobli of Anekal, Bagalur village in Jala hobli, and Bommashettihalli and Giddenahalli villages in Dasanapura hobli.
The minister said notices have also been affixed to over 2,000 abandoned vehicles asking their owners to come forward and take them back. Vehicles for which there has been no response are now being towed.
KBG questions civic spending, work quality
At a Bengaluru urban zilla panchayat Karnataka Development Programme meeting Wednesday, Byre Gowda questioned officials over the quality of civic work and the utilisation of funds by gram panchayats.
Questioning the repeated demand for funds to repair roads, the minister said a properly constructed road should last several years. He questioned whether Karnataka was spending less on road construction than other states and rejected explanations that traffic, vehicle density and rainfall were responsible for poor road durability.
“If the work is done properly and a road lasts at least eight years, the money spent is justified. But if it gets damaged every two years, no amount of money will be enough,” he said.
He also stressed that a portion of funds sanctioned to gram panchayats must be mandatorily used for permanent infrastructure, including drinking water, sewerage treatment plants, and electrical crematoriums.

stories.headline: Anthropic quietly sets up biology lab for AI drug project
stories.bodyText:
SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic has set up a wet lab in San Francisco Bay Area, expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions into physical biology and drug science, according to two people familiar with the matter and company life sciences head Eric Kauderer-Abrams.
The Dario Amodei-led startup has said it wants to unlock treatments for rare diseases, taking its biology work beyond computer evaluations. A spokesperson said the lab was not specifically for drug discovery but declined to elaborate. "We believe that to do biology, the final test is still and will be for a while in real lab work," Kauderer-Abrams said. He said Anthropic conducted some work in its facilities and some with external partners.
Anthropic wants its Claude AI to direct robotic units conducting experiments with limited human intervention, a source said. Its spokesperson said human involvement remained essential for safety.
"In our life-science work, we're always balancing these things," Kauderer-Abrams said, "making models better in ways that we think will uplift and accelerate developing medicines, and being thoughtful about how we deploy it to limit the risk."
Anthropic said in June it planned preclinical work in areas traditional companies found financially unattractive. It launched Claude Science, added Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan to its board and acquired Coefficient Bio for about $400 million in stock, according to media reports. Anthropic confirmed the acquisition but not the price.
The company is expanding in-house laboratory work for speed and firsthand biology experience, while outsourcing where efficient. Job advertisements indicate it is hiring for procurement and operations as well as protein and nucleic acid characterisation. Life sciences is already among its biggest investment areas by staff.
Anthropic believes AI could accelerate work on previously "undruggable" conditions, including development of complex antibodies. However, the diseases targeted and its progress remain unclear. It is not conducting clinical trials for now, focusing on needs industry would not address. Reuters

stories.headline: Trump extends H-1B visa restrictions, including $100,000 payment requirement, for another year
stories.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump has extended restrictions on the H-1B nonimmigrant visa programme for another 12 months, keeping in place a $100,000 payment requirement for certain H-1B workers seeking to enter the US.
The White House said in a proclamation signed on Friday that the restrictions imposed in September 2025 would be extended until September 21, 2027. The administration said the move was necessary because the conditions that led to the original restrictions “persist”.
“On September 19, 2025, Proclamation 10973 (Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers) (2025 Proclamation), was issued to address significant abuses of the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program,” the proclamation said.
“The restrictions enacted by the 2025 Proclamation have proven to be highly effective but the underlying conditions necessitating the restrictions persist,” it added.
Under the extended policy, the entry of H-1B specialty occupation workers covered by the proclamation will remain restricted unless their petitions are accompanied or supplemented by a $100,000 payment. The restriction applies to workers who are outside the US and seek to enter the country after September 21, 2026.
There are limited exceptions. The secretary of Homeland Security can exempt an individual, a company's workers or workers in an industry if their hiring is determined to be in the US national interest and not a threat to the country's security or welfare.
The Trump administration has argued that the H-1B system has been exploited by some employers, particularly IT staffing and outsourcing firms, to replace American workers with lower-paid foreign labour.
The proclamation said the policy had already produced a sharp change in H-1B filings. According to the White House, combined H-1B registrations by the largest IT staffing and outsourcing firms fell from 24,946 to 2,055, a 92% decline. It also said consular processing requests fell by nearly 97% between the FY2025 and FY2027 cap seasons.
The White House also cited a shift towards higher-skilled and higher-paid applicants, saying registrations for beneficiaries with at least a US master's degree rose from 45.1% of total registrants for FY2026 to 66.1% for FY2027.
The proclamation further said the administration would continue to review the policy, with senior officials required to recommend whether another extension or renewal would be in the US interest after the next H-1B lottery.

stories.headline: What does the latest revision to the EPFO wage ceiling entail? | Explained
stories.deck: How does the EPFO wage ceiling revision expand the social security net? What are the concerns of Unions and Employers? What are the legal issues that may arise?
stories.bodyText:
The story so far: The Union Cabinet, which met in New Delhi on Wednesday (September 16, 2026), approved a long-pending demand for raising the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to ₹25,000 a month from ₹15,000. The Union Labour Ministry had made the proposal to increase the wage ceiling. The last time the ceiling was increased was in September 2014. The employers’ organisations, largely, welcomed the announcement and sought the Union Government’s help to implement the decision as the employers’ share to the Provident Fund will increase. The trade unions described the increase as “too little and too late”.
The Government said in a release that the decision reflects the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the years. On Thursday (September 17, 2026) the Union Labour Ministry published an official gazette notification maintaining that the decision was taken based on Clause (89) of Section 2 of the Code on Social Security.
Expanding the Social Security Net
The Union Government said the decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers. Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya told reporters that about one crore subscribers could be added to the ambit of the EPFO by the decision.
He said the average salary in private establishments has increased up to ₹ 23,000 as per Government survey and increasing the ceiling is a decision based on that. Other than the access to the retirement fund savings, which has a higher interest rate compared to other small saving schemes, the new decision will also help a number of workers to access pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI).
The Government will spend about ₹11,339 crore towards its contribution to the EPS, against the existing annual budgetary support of about ₹10,250 crore. The Government maintained that the measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. “By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection,” it added.
Contributions to the Fund
The contributions of the employees and employers towards the Provident Fund and to the Employees Pension Scheme will also increase as per the new wage ceiling. Employers’ contribution to the PF will increase by ₹600 per employee and the new contribution rate for EPS will be ₹2,082.5 (8.33% of the new ceiling) per month, from the present amount of ₹1,250.
For the employees, the contribution to PF is 12% of the wages (basic and dearness allowance). According to the Code on Wages, the wage is calculated as basic+DA+retainable allowances. For employers, the contribution is 3.67% of the wages towards the PF and 8.33% (capped at ₹ 1,250 now, which will go up to ₹ 2,082.5) towards the EPS. According to the latest EPFO data, it has around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners and the EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership. The employer also pays 0.5% towards the EDLI and another 0.5% as administration charges.
Concerns of Unions and Employers
All India Trade Union Congress general secretary Amarjeet Kaur said the decision was too little and too late. She expressed concern over the protection of take-home pay of the employees. Her argument was that the benefit of expansion of social security should not be at the cost of reduced monthly pay packet.
“The employer’s statutory EPFO contribution must be paid over and above the employee’s cost to the company and should not be deducted from or adjusted against the employee’s agreed and existing wages,” she said in a statement and demanded that a regular and automatic mechanism for periodic revision of the EPFO wage ceiling may be established, instead of waiting for another decade or more and responding only after sustained trade-union pressure.
National chairman of the Association of Indian Entrepreneurs (AIE) K.E. Raghunathan said employers, especially MSMEs, would find it very tough to absorb the additional strain on their outflow, especially when most of them are struggling to make any profit. “This should not discourage them from formal employment and instead go for gig working arrangements. The Government of India must absorb this increase for two years in the case of MSMEs,” he said.
Legal issues
Anand Gopalan, a Chennai-based lawyer, argues that the Government should consider implementing the enhanced ceiling from April 1, 2027 rather than with immediate effect. “If the ceiling is enhanced to ₹25,000, the employee’s contribution would increase to ₹3,000 per month — an increase of ₹1,200 every month.”
“For an employee earning around ₹25,000 per month, a reduction of additional ₹1,200 in monthly take-home pay would be a significant impact on his day-to-day finances. If employees are informed in advance that the change will take effect from April 2027, they would have sufficient time to plan and arrange their finances accordingly,” he said, adding that the EPFO would need to make the necessary system and administrative changes to implement the revised ceiling.
“The objective of expanding social security coverage is certainly important. At the same time, the transition should take into account the practical financial and administrative difficulties that may be faced by both employees and employers,” he added.

stories.headline: No hard ceilings: On the revision to EPFO wage ceiling
stories.deck: A rise in minimum PF pension will protect the worse-off among the retired
stories.bodyText:
The Union Cabinet’s approval to raise the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000, though belated, is commendable. The BJP-led government has finally responded to this long-standing demand of workers in the organised sector. Around 51 lakh additional employees may be brought under the PF fold, which has around 7.98 crore contributing members. Those in the wage slab of ₹15,000-₹25,000 will now be covered under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS), 2026. Although Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya cited a government survey as the basis for the increase, the 12-year delay in implementing it should have been avoided. The Minister, who said that the average salary in private establishments was ₹23,000, should also make the survey’s findings public for a better understanding of the country’s overall wage situation. With some concerns having been raised that not every employer may be willing to make the additional contributions required after the revision, the government must ensure that all employers comply with the law.
So far, the government has been silent on revising the EPS minimum pension of ₹1,000, fixed in September 2014 alongside the previous revision in the PF wage ceiling. EPFO pensioners have been demanding the hike in the minimum pension amount. Before it assumed office at the Centre in 2014, the BJP had urged the Congress-led UPA government to keep the minimum pension at ₹3,000 and index it to inflation. Yet, it has not made even a symbolic beginning towards the indexation of pension to inflation. Moreover, about 45% of the nearly 82 lakh pensioners receive ₹1,000 or less. In March 2026, the Joint Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour reminded the government that “the existing minimum pension amount is inadequate to meet even the basic needs of pensioners particularly in the ... scenario marked by ... rising healthcare and living expenses”. Also, little is known about the follow-up to the panel’s recommendation for “an urgent and comprehensive review of the minimum pension”. The EPFO must release the findings of actuarial assessment, made by valuers in recent years. briefs.headline: Shapoorji Pallonji Group, with 18.4% Tata Sons stake, backs its public listing
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: A day after Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata warned that a listing "will destroy" 
Tata Sons
' character and "strike at the heart" of an operating model that "has stood the test of time for more than a century", Shapoorji Pallonji Group (SPG) chairman Shapoor Mistry took the contrary view, describing a public listing as a "social and moral imperative" and deepening a rare public rift between two of the company's largest shareholders.
Mistry, whose conglomerate holds an 18.4% stake in Tata Sons, said the "path forward is clear" after Reserve Bank Of India rejected the company's application to surrender its registration and directed it to comply with regulations.
Before the RBI decision, brothers-in-law Noel and Mistry had explored a settlement under which SP would monetise part of its Tata Sons holding for Rs 25,000 crore. Noel had even tabled a proposal at Thursday's board meeting, which he said came from SPG. The offer made in a letter - before RBI's Sept 11 order mandating an 
IPO
 - entailed Tata Sons buying out shares held by SPG's investment firms, Sterling Investment Corporation and Cyrus Investments, in two tranches.
The talks evidently failed to yield an agreement due to differences over the valuation of SPG's stake in Tata Sons. Typically, a holding company is valued by the stock market at a discount to the total worth of its investments in group companies. Mistry's statement on Friday made no mention of differences between the two sides in arriving at the right price.
An IPO, on the other hand, would provide SP more leverage and liquidity to pare debt and help unlock value for shares whose stakes have long been tied to Tata Sons' private status.
Mistry cast the RBI ruling on Tata Sons as an opening for reconciliation, not conflict. "This should not be viewed as a victory of one stakeholder over another," he said. "It should be viewed as an opportunity to bring people and institutions together."
Despite the often fraught history between the two groups, their century-old relationship had endured, Mistry said, because it was "rooted in something larger than individual interests."
'NextGen should inherit not a legacy of division, but a legacy of cooperation' | page 23
The public listing of Tata Sons is "not merely a financial or regulatory matter. It is a social and moral imperative," Mistry said.
The RBI decision marked a "pivotal moment not merely for Tata Sons, but for the principles of transparency, accountability, fairness and responsible institution-building that should guide enterprises of national importance", Mistry said. He lauded the "exemplary leadership" of PM Modi, "particularly his commitment to strengthening institutions and enabling them to discharge their responsibilities with clarity, authority and purpose", referring to the "govt's stated respect for RBI's autonomy".
SPG became a substantial stakeholder in Tata Sons through a series of purchases starting in the 1930s and going up to the 90s involving sale of shares by descendants of the Tata Group founder as well as others. "I believe the next generation should inherit not a legacy of division, but a legacy of cooperation," Mistry said. "There is a great deal that the Shapoorji Pallonji and Tata institutions do and can continue to do together."
He urged Tata Sons, Tata Trusts and other stakeholders to approach a listing in a "spirit of harmony and shared purpose." "Let us not allow the listing to become even a minor point of division. Let us use it as an opportunity for reconciliation." He added that he wanted to work "closely and constructively" with Tata Sons toward that end.
A listed Tata Sons, Mistry said, would broaden participation in the company, improve governance, provide greater visibility on value, and pave the way for a more equitable dividend policy while protecting investors' interests.
Invoking Tata founder Jamsetji Tata, Mistry argued the group's next chapter should place community and nation-building at the centre of enterprise, directly contesting Noel's framing. "The question before us should not simply be who owns what, or how a corporate structure is preserved," he said. "The larger question should be how one of India's greatest industrial institutions can become even stronger, more transparent, more accountable and more capable."

Funds diverted, says CBI

briefs.headline: MDR apprehension unlikely to spur higher cash usage: RBI Deputy Governor
briefs.deck: From October 15, a 0.4% MDR will apply to person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000. The charge will be paid by merchants, not consumers, and will be capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 or more
briefs.bodyText:
Concerns that introducing a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) would spur a surge in cash transactions are unlikely to materialise, RBI Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said on Friday (September 18, 2026), adding that it was only an “initial apprehension”.
From October 15, a 0.4% MDR will apply to person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000. The charge will be paid by merchants, not consumers, and will be capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 or more.
Payments between individuals, as well as the vast majority of everyday merchant payments, will remain free.
“I don’t think that apprehension will come true. It will be just initial apprehension,” Mr. Murmu said while addressing a financial market conclave hosted here by BCC&I on whether more cash would be used because of MDR.
“Because it is a major shift in terms of how basically you are recovering the cost. So, that’s why it may be apprehension only. I don’t think this will have any impact, unlike some voices about whether cash will go up because of this MDR.” On the apparent paradox of rising digital transactions and cash in circulation, Mr. Murmu said there was no paradox, as cash serves both as a means of transaction and a store of value.
Also read: Complex priorities: On UPI transactions, MDR charges
“This cash paradox, actually, is not my work. That is the way the media has read it, and analysis has read it. Because it points towards data,” he said.
“But I can tell you, if you look at it closely, it’s no paradox. We are looking at cash in circulation, particularly notes in circulation. How it is getting impacted as digital currency is taking up,” he added.
Mr. Murmu pointed out that the expectation that cash in circulation should correspondingly decline as digital transactions increase was not borne out by the data because two things were happening simultaneously.
On the RBI’s recent regulatory changes, Mr. Murmu said the central bank had issued more than 600 draft and final amendment circulars in the last year.
“We have, in fact, if you count, you take a simple count of the number of draft circulars we have issued, and the final amendment circulars; in the last year it will be more than 600,” he said.
However, Mr. Murmu said, the number should not be seen as a measure of the regulatory burden on individual entities, as the RBI had reorganised its regulations across different categories of regulated entities.
“So, don’t get intimidated by the number. Because of what we have done, we have reclassified all our regulated entities into some 11 categories. So, some of the circulars are basically a multiple of 11,” he said.
He said the exercise was aimed at reducing the compliance burden for regulated entities.
“So, from a regulated entity point of view, we are reducing their burden, and that burden we have shifted towards us,” Mr. Murmu said.
On the RBI’s shift towards principle-based regulation, Murmu said it was not a complete move away from rule-based regulation.
“See, when we say we are basically moving towards as much as possible principle-based, but you cannot give up your rule-based also. See, it’s a balance,” he said.
On the increasing use of artificial intelligence by banks and financial institutions, Mr. Murmu said accountability would continue to rest with boards even if machines replaced or supplemented human decision-making.
“At the end of the point, what I was making in my speech was that irrespective of whether machines replace humans or supplement them, the accountability will rest with boards,” he said.
He said boards would have to educate themselves as financial institutions increasingly moved from human intelligence to machine intelligence.

briefs.headline: NSE’s ₹22,569-crore IPO fully subscribed on Day 2
briefs.deck: The offering is India’s second-largest public issue after Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,870-crore IPO in 2024
briefs.bodyText:
The ₹22,569-crore initial public offering of the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) was fully subscribed on the second day of bidding on Friday (September 18, 2026), driven by encouraging response from non-institutional investors and qualified institutional buyers.
The offering is India’s second-largest public issue after Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,870-crore IPO in 2024. The IPO surpassed the ₹21,000 crore offering of LIC in 2022 but remains below Hyundai Motor India’s record public offer.
The NSE IPO received bids for 10,28,43,656 shares against 8,86,42,911 shares on offer, garnering 1.16 times subscription, as per data available with the BSE.
Non-institutional investors and qualified institutional buyers categories drew full subscriptions on the second day.
The category for non-institutional investors was subscribed 1.68 times, while the portion for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) received 1.53 subscriptions. The retail investors’ quota received 72% subscription.
The NSE on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) raised ₹6,746 crore from anchor investors, including state-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Goldman Sachs and Fidelity.
Additionally, sovereign wealth funds such as GIC Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) and Norges Bank, as well as Eastspring and HSBC Global Asset Management, also participated in the anchor round.
The IPO comprises an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 12.64 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.
The exchange has fixed a price band of ₹1,700-1,785 per equity share for the IPO. It will command a valuation of up to ₹4.42 lakh crore at the upper end of the price band.
The issue will close on September 21.
Since the offering is entirely an OFS, the proceeds from the share sale will accrue to the existing shareholders and not to the NSE.
The public issue marks a significant milestone for the NSE, whose listing plans had remained stalled for nearly a decade amid regulatory hurdles, including those linked to the co-location controversy.
The reduction in the OFS size from the earlier planned 14.9 crore shares has brought down the overall issue size from the initial estimate of around ₹30,000 crore.
NSE shares are expected to make their market debut on September 24.

briefs.headline: RBI may deliver two rate hikes by CY 2026:Analysts
briefs.deck: The combination of elevated inflation risks, strong liquidity conditions and a potential global tightening cycle is prompting expectations that the RBI may shift towards a more restrictive monetary stance in the second half of 2026.
briefs.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is likely to raise the repo rate twice by as much as 50 basis points by the end of December 2026 in line with global tightening cycle and excess liquidity in the banking system.
Market participants expect the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to deliver a 25 basis point rate hike in October 2026, followed by another 25 basis point increase in December, taking the benchmark repo rate to 6% by the end of the calendar year. One basis point is equal to one-hundredth of a percentage point.
The anticipated tightening comes amid concerns that inflation could exceed the RBI’s earlier projections, particularly if crude oil prices remain elevated.
“Incoming data suggests inflation is likely to overshoot those projections. If crude prices stay elevated in the $90-$110/barrel range, the pass-through from producer costs to final output prices is likely to accelerate,” Systematix Group said in a report.
“Against the prevailing 5.25% repo rate, it effectively implies a negative real policy rate — precisely the “cheap money” condition we had warned was unsustainable,” it added.
India’s retail inflation rose to 4.82% in August 2026 from 4.45% in July, while economists expect September inflation to approach the 5% mark.
A key factor influencing the RBI’s policy stance is the substantial liquidity surplus created by foreign currency inflows, particularly through the special non-resident deposit scheme. Analysts estimate that around $127 billion in FCNR(B) inflows have contributed significantly to the banking system’s liquidity surplus.
“FCNR(B) inflows have created a core liquidity surplus of ₹15 trillion. Excess liquidity can quickly become inflationary and can raise financial stability risks if banks become dependent on abundant liquidity,” HSBC said in a report.
The central bank has already deployed multiple liquidity management tools, including open market operations (OMOs) and variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions, to absorb surplus funds from the banking system.
Analysts expect the RBI to intensify its absorption measures in the coming months. Through VRRR operations and other instruments, the central bank is expected to withdraw an additional ₹4 lakh crore of liquidity, over and above the nearly ₹2.5 lakh crore already absorbed.
